claims.text: Protective oxide formation in high-temperature HEAs is governed by preferential enrichment and controlled oxidation of protective elements such as Al and Cr.
Alumina and chromia are the primary protective oxides formed on AlCoCrFeNi-type HEAs at elevated temperature.
Preferential oxidation of Al and Cr produces a continuous and adherent oxide scale.
The alumina/chromia scale slows oxygen ingress and thereby reduces oxidation kinetics.
The initial AlCoCrFeNi-type HEA has a homogeneously distributed microstructure.
Increasing bulk Al and/or Cr content relative to a reduced-content HEA control will promote formation of the protective scale.
Oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi has been evaluated over approximately 850–1050 °C.
Grain boundaries facilitate transport of protective elements to the surface.
Chemical complexity intrinsic to HEAs causes diffusion kinetics to favor selective migration and oxidation of protective elements.
Al and Cr form thermodynamically stable, slow-growing oxides.
The multi-element matrix minimizes rapid depletion of protective elements and prevents formation of non-protective porous oxides.
An HEA enriched in Al and/or Cr will have lower weight gain and slower oxide growth than an otherwise comparable reduced-content HEA.
An HEA enriched in protective elements will form a more continuous, adherent, and chemically uniform oxide scale than the reduced-content control.
A coarser microstructure is expected to hinder selective diffusion, produce a less protective oxide scale, and increase oxidation rate.
The proposed behavior applies approximately from 850 to 1050 °C in oxidative atmospheres.
The behavior may differ at substantially higher temperatures, in reducing atmospheres, or in alloys lacking Al and Cr.
Failure of the enriched samples to form a continuous alumina/chromia scale and achieve a statistically lower oxidation rate than the reduced-content control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The controlled comparison is said to have identical processing and microstructural characteristics except for protective-element content, but the baseline also permits a coarser microstructure. Allowing grain size to vary would confound the proposed composition-only comparison.
